CVE-2026-123125.title: Symfony: Ip Constraint public/private Modes Accept IPv4-Mapped and IPv4-Compatible IPv6 Addresses allowing SSRF Filter Bypass
CVE-2026-123125.description:
The Symfony Validator component IpValidator incompletely classifies internal addresses in the filtered modes of the Ip constraint, so some internal addresses are accepted as public, which can lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.

In these modes, IpValidator relies on the PHP flags FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE and FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE to classify addresses as public, private, or reserved. These flags do not cover shared address space (100.64.0.0/10) or IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, and 6to4 IPv6 addresses, which can embed internal IPv4 addresses. A value such as ::ffff:127.0.0.1 can therefore pass validation even though it points to an internal host.
Applications that rely on the Ip constraint to reject internal addresses, for example before making a server-side request to a user-supplied address, can be exposed to SSRF.

CVE-2026-42271.title: LiteLLM: Authenticated command execution via MCP stdio test endpoints
CVE-2026-42271.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.74.2 to before version 1.83.7, two endpoints used to preview an MCP server before saving it — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — accepted a full server configuration in the request body, including the command, args, and env fields used by the stdio transport. CVE-2026-99125.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/pai: Handle multiple PMU stop callback invocations

Handle the following scenario:
The kernel protects itself against a very high sampling load and
throttles the sampling using:

perf_event_throttle() --> PMU->stop()

Shortly later the scheduler may terminate the task and removes it from the
CPU. It again calls

PMU->stop()

which results in two invocations of PMU->stop() called back to back.
Protect against this and check the PERF_HES_STOPPED bit on function
entry. If it is already set return.
Clear bit PERF_HES_STOPPED in PMU->start().

Prohibit ioctl(fd, PERF_EVENT_IOC_PERIOD, ...) call for this event.
It sets perf_event::event_limit to a positive value and causes
perf_event_overflow() to invoke pai_stop() call back function when
perf_event::event_limit hits zero. This is not supported because the
sample events CRYPTO_ALL and NNPA_ALL are only taken at schedule out
of a task.

Use list_for_each_entry_safe()…

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir

Listing a directory while it is copied up causes a use-after-free of
the readdir cache.

A merge directory must never be iterated as a real upper directory:
that mode frees the cache in OVL_I(inode)->cache without looking at
its refcount, while files opened in merged mode still use it.
ovl_copy_up_workdir() publishes the upper dentry before it sets
OVL_WHITEOUTS, and ovl_dir_open() samples both without a lock, so an
open between the two stores finds the upper directory and takes it
for a real one.

listed a directory during its copy-up saw only "." and "..", and its
next getdents freed the readdir cache of another descriptor.

CVE-2026-99675.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: reject keep-alive timeouts that would overflow

nvmet_set_feat_kato() and nvmet_alloc_ctrl() convert the 32-bit
millisecond KATO from the host to seconds with DIV_ROUND_UP(kato, 1000).
The addition in DIV_ROUND_UP() is done in 32 bits, so any KATO above
4294966296 ms wraps around and rounds to 0 seconds. A Set Features
command with KATO 0xffffffff then succeeds but disables the keep-alive
timer: Get Features returns 0 and Keep Alive fails with Keep Alive

without a keep-alive timer.

multiplies it by 1000, and the timer paths multiply it by HZ in 32 bits
and arm a delay that must not exceed MAX_JIFFY_OFFSET.

Alive Timeout Invalid from both Set Features and Connect. Validate Set

CVE-2026-99741.title: tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id
CVE-2026-99741.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tmpfs: keep the quota soft limits of an unused id

When the last reference to a dquot goes away, shmem_release_dquot()
stores its limits in the rb tree of the mount, unless
shmem_is_empty_dquot() says that there is nothing worth storing. That
function looks at the usage and at the two hard limits only.

So if the administrator sets nothing but soft limits for an id that owns
no file yet, the entry is thrown away as soon as the dquot that
Q_SETQUOTA used is released, and the id never gets to see a limit.

To fix it, compare the soft limits as well: an entry can be empty only if
both soft limits are zero as well, which is exactly what
shmem_acquire_dquot() sets for a new entry.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

CVE-2026-99802.title: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()
CVE-2026-99802.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()

When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches
directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking
current->io_uring_restrict.

As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via
IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes
such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in
the task's allowed register_op bitmap.

Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in
io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.
